newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Southern says Circle buy to be EPS positive.
newsitem.headline: Southern says Circle buy to be EPS positive.

text.p: Film and television production company Southern Star Group Ltd said on Tuesday that its recent purchase of Circle Communications of Britain would be earnings per share positive in the year to March 31, 1998.

"We expect the acquisition of Circle to be earnings per share positive by the end of this financial year as well as positioning the company for strong growth in the years ahead," chairman Neil Balnaves told the annual meeting.
Southern Star bought the London-based television rights group for 9.8 million stg in June. Balnaves said the purchase gave the group more growth opportunities over the next decade.
Circle has a library of over 1,000 hours of programming and operates the Oxford Scientific Films business.

"Already we have taken steps to expand Circle's other activities. The company has already acquired two more series for distribution and is in negotiations with other producers to join the company," Balnaves said.
Balnaves said the group would open on Wednesday its new optical disc manufacturing plant, capable of producing CD's, CD ROM's and ultimately digital video discs.
He said the group was negotiating manufacturing agreements with Polygram, Microsoft, Disney, Paramount and Universal.
Southern Group reported a net profit of A$10.16 million for the year to March 31, 1997, compared with A$12.40 million a year earlier. The group listed on the stock exchange in September 1996.
At 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT), Southern Group shares were four cents down A$1.70.
